selectedCognition.title: 10.7 内在视觉：当理解先在你的内部形成画面
selectedCognition.text: 你的人类图在 Cognition（认知感官）这一层，对应 Inner Vision（内在视觉）。这组传统分类把阅读带向一种与内部图像和整体印象有关的经验：有时，别人还在逐项说明一件事情，你的理解却可能先以画面、空间关系或某种完整场景的形式逐渐成形。你可能更容易先想象一件事情完成后的轮廓，再回头寻找组成它的步骤；也可能在安静下来之后，才发现白天接收到的零散信息开始彼此连接。对你来说，一项认识未必总是从第一句话开始建立，有时候它先是一幅还没有被完全说清楚的内部地图。

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 内在视觉：当理解先在你的内部形成画面
selectedCognition.text: 这种方式可以在学习、创作和解决问题时提供另一种切入点。例如，当你准备调整一项工作流程，脑海中可能先出现不同部门如何交接、哪些环节互相影响的整体图景。你知道自己想要改善什么，却未必马上知道怎样把它解释给别人。此时，把想法画成流程、安排成步骤，或借助具体例子向别人说明，能够让内部形成的理解逐渐进入可以讨论和检验的现实。你的优势不一定只是拥有画面，而是能够在适当的时候，将它整理成别人也能参与的表达方式。

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 内在视觉：当理解先在你的内部形成画面
selectedCognition.text: 你也可能注意到，持续受到声音、讯息或他人要求打断时，自己不容易完成这个整理过程。有些想法需要一段不必立即回应的时间，才有机会发展出更清楚的结构。你可以在条件允许时，先记录脑海中出现的关键词、关系或草图，再决定哪些值得继续研究。但也不需要强迫自己一定看见清晰影像：有些人体验到的是空间关系、顺序感或整体印象。无论呈现方式如何，内部形成的画面与直觉都可以是探索的起点，重要的判断仍要回到实际证据、相关人的反馈和可验证的结果。

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 内在视觉：当理解先在你的内部形成画面
selectedCognition.text: 当 Inner Vision 与你其他已确认的配置一起阅读时，它可以帮助你更具体地认识：什么情况下想法会自然成形，什么时候适合把它转换为语言，以及哪些认识值得进一步投入实践。你不必急于把每个内部画面变成行动，也不必因为别人暂时不明白，就否定自己的理解。让内部形成的想法拥有恰当的表达和验证过程，正是这项认知主题可以进入日常生活的方式。

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Inner Vision: When Understanding Takes Shape Within You
selectedCognition.text: Your Human Design Cognition is classified as Inner Vision. In the traditional framework, this brings attention to the way images, spatial relationships and an overall sense of a situation may take shape internally. At times, other people may still be explaining a problem step by step while you are beginning to imagine how its parts belong together. You might picture the eventual outcome before knowing exactly how to describe the path toward it, or discover that disconnected details begin to make more sense once you have a quieter moment to consider them. Understanding does not always begin as a complete sentence. Sometimes it starts as an internal outline that has yet to find its language.

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Inner Vision: When Understanding Takes Shape Within You
selectedCognition.text: This perspective may feel especially relevant when you are learning, creating or improving a process. Imagine reviewing a workflow that involves several people. You might first form an overall impression of how information moves between them and where the sequence could be simpler. Explaining that picture to others is a separate task. A sketch, a process map or a concrete example can help translate what you have imagined into something that other people can examine and test. The potential strength is not merely having an internal image, but learning when and how to make that understanding accessible and useful.

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Inner Vision: When Understanding Takes Shape Within You
selectedCognition.text: You may also notice that constant interruptions leave little room to organize an impression fully. Sometimes a short interval without new demands is enough to return to an idea with more clarity. Writing down relationships, drawing a rough diagram or revisiting a question later may provide a helpful bridge. You do not need to force yourself to see vivid mental pictures: for some people, the experience may be closer to recognizing an arrangement, a sequence or a whole. Whatever form it takes, an internal impression can be a starting point for exploration; reliable conclusions still benefit from evidence, feedback and practical testing.

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Inner Vision: When Understanding Takes Shape Within You
selectedCognition.text: Read alongside the other verified elements of your chart, Inner Vision can offer a more personal way to consider when ideas begin to cohere, how you communicate them and which possibilities deserve further attention. You do not have to turn every inner picture into a task or assume that a lack of immediate agreement makes your understanding less valuable. Allowing an idea to develop, find clear expression and meet reality gives this theme a practical place in everyday life.

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Feeling / 感觉
selectedCognition.text: 你的 Cognition 在传统分类中称为感觉。你可以从一段体验的整体感受来探索它：某种节奏、环境或互动，是否让自己更安定、紧绷或容易分心。把当时的条件与感受一起记录，能够帮助区别持续存在的因素与某一次困难的时刻。

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Feeling / 感觉
selectedCognition.text: 感受值得被注意，但不必因此成为不可质疑的判断。可以同时比较睡眠、工作量、预期及现实任务要求。重要选择仍须结合内在权威的过程、可靠资料和适当意见。这一分类不诊断身体状况，也不证明能够直接读取别人的情绪。

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Feeling / 感觉
selectedCognition.text: Your Cognition is traditionally described as Feeling. This can be explored as attention to the overall felt quality of an experience: whether a pace, setting or interaction leaves you more settled, strained or distracted. Recording the circumstances alongside the feeling helps distinguish a recurring condition from a difficult moment.

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Feeling / 感觉
selectedCognition.text: A feeling deserves attention without becoming an unquestionable verdict. Compare sleep, workload, expectations and the practical demands of the situation. For important decisions, combine your chart’s Authority process with reliable information and appropriate advice. This classification does not diagnose a condition or establish that you can read another person’s emotions.

selectedCognition.text: 你的 Cognition 在传统分类中称为味觉。你可以从直接体验中的细微区别来探索这一主题：先尝试一个可逆的小选择，注意它与另一种选择具体有什么不同，再决定是否继续。例如，比较两种工具或两份作品时，把自己重视的细节说清楚，会比只说好或不好更有帮助。

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Taste / 味觉
selectedCognition.text: 个人偏好不是衡量品质的普遍标准。可以把喜欢的特点与任务要求分开，也容许别人有不同偏好。这一阅读不提供食物、饮食或医疗处方，更不把一时喜欢当成作出重大承诺的充分依据。

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Taste / 味觉
selectedCognition.text: Your Cognition is traditionally described as Taste. A useful way to explore this theme is through careful distinctions in direct experience: trying a small, reversible option, noticing what actually differs and deciding what deserves another attempt. Comparing two versions of a tool or a piece of work can make your preferences more specific than simply calling one good and the other bad.

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Taste / 味觉
selectedCognition.text: Personal preference is not a universal measure of quality. Name the feature you value, compare it with the requirements of the task and allow other people to have different preferences. This reading does not prescribe food, a diet or a medical regimen, and it does not make a momentary liking sufficient evidence for a major commitment.

selectedCognition.text: 你的 Cognition 在传统分类中称为味觉。你可以从直接体验中的细微区别来探索这一主题：先尝试一个可逆的小选择，注意它与另一种选择具体有什么不同，再决定是否继续。例如，比较两种工具或两份作品时，把自己重视的细节说清楚，会比只说好或不好更有帮助。

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Taste / 味觉
selectedCognition.text: Your Cognition is traditionally described as Taste. A useful way to explore this theme is through careful distinctions in direct experience: trying a small, reversible option, noticing what actually differs and deciding what deserves another attempt. Comparing two versions of a tool or a piece of work can make your preferences more specific than simply calling one good and the other bad.

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Taste / 味觉

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Feeling / 感觉
selectedCognition.text: 你的 Cognition 在传统分类中称为感觉。你可以从一段体验的整体感受来探索它：某种节奏、环境或互动，是否让自己更安定、紧绷或容易分心。把当时的条件与感受一起记录，能够帮助区别持续存在的因素与某一次困难的时刻。

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Feeling / 感觉
selectedCognition.text: 感受值得被注意，但不必因此成为不可质疑的判断。可以同时比较睡眠、工作量、预期及现实任务要求。重要选择仍须结合内在权威的过程、可靠资料和适当意见。这一分类不诊断身体状况，也不证明能够直接读取别人的情绪。

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Feeling / 感觉
selectedCognition.text: Your Cognition is traditionally described as Feeling. This can be explored as attention to the overall felt quality of an experience: whether a pace, setting or interaction leaves you more settled, strained or distracted. Recording the circumstances alongside the feeling helps distinguish a recurring condition from a difficult moment.

selectedCognition.title: 10.7 Feeling / 感觉
selectedCognition.text: A feeling deserves attention without becoming an unquestionable verdict. Compare sleep, workload, expectations and the practical demands of the situation. For important decisions, combine your chart’s Authority process with reliable information and appropriate advice. This classification does not diagnose a condition or establish that you can read another person’s emotions.
